text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent midweek newspapers, The Sun and The Gazette, on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The ruling Botswana Democratic Party (BDP) unexpectedly wins two by-elections in the Maun/Chobe constituency. BDP youth leader and MP for the area, Jacob Nkate said: "In what initially appeared to be a case of working against considerable odds, we did well." The area is in Ngamiland, where farmers have seen almost all their cattle destroyed in the campaign to eradicate cattle lung disease.

- The newly formed Botswana Insurance Brokers' Association has registered 12 broking firms. The Registrar of Insurance has to clear financial status, experience in the business and technical capabilities before applicants are accepted.

- Management of Information Trust Corporation Botswana, a subsidiary of ITC South Africa, and minority shareholder the Botswana Development Corporation (BDC) are called to the Office of the President to explain a recent furore over adverse reports of the way in which the credit bureau works.
ITC was recently criticised by Radio Botswana and local newspapers for allegedly allowing unfair credit reports to remain on its books and to be available to subscribers.
Several cabinet ministers have reportedly called for the bureau to be closed and are said to have the support of the President.
